concepts.def: A fundamental particle (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom) that makes up hadrons.
A fundamental particle not subject to the strong interaction; includes the electron, muon and neutrinos.
A composite particle made of quarks; subdivided into baryons (3 quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).
Boson mediating a fundamental force, e.g. photon (EM), W/Z (weak), gluon (strong).
A neutron decays to a proton, electron and antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e.
In particle interactions, charge, baryon number, lepton number and energy/momentum are conserved.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Particles & Medical Physics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Particles & Medical Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Particles & Medical Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A proton consists of which quarks?
options: udd
uud
uds
uuu

mcqs.q: In β⁻ decay, the exchange particle is:
options: Photon
W⁻ boson
Gluon
Z boson

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a fundamental particle: proton, electron, or neutron?
options: No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
Only the electron — protons and neutrons are made of quarks.
All three (proton, electron, neutron) are fundamental particles that cannot be broken down.

mcqs.q: Is the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies a true Doppler shift?
options: No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Yes — it is the same Doppler shift as a moving siren on Earth.
No — it arises from the expansion of space stretching photon wavelengths during transit, not from the galaxy's motion through space.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.

mcqs.q: Was the Big Bang an explosion of matter into pre-existing space?
options: Yes — it was a giant explosion at a point, and galaxies are still flying outwards from it.
No — it was the expansion of space itself, beginning from a hot dense state; there was no 'outside' for matter to expand into.
No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Yes — it was a bomb-like event that destroyed an earlier universe.
